about.title: Palm Desert Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Palm Desert draws steady foot traffic to its resorts, golf clubs, and retail centers along Highway 111 and El Paseo, and with that traffic comes spills, uneven pavement, and poorly maintained walkways. When a property owner fails to address a known hazard, the people who fall on their premises can be left with real injuries and mounting medical bills. Under California law, proving a premises liability claim generally means showing the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and didn't fix it or warn visitors in time. That's why documenting the scene, photographing the hazard, and asking the property to preserve any surveillance footage matters so much in Riverside County claims. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves, we simply connect injured Palm Desert residents and visitors with an independent attorney who can evaluate the notice evidence and pursue the claim on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Evidence Matter in Your Claim

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises liability claims hinge on showing the property owner had notice of the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help identify inspection logs, maintenance records, and prior complaints that establish this notice.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Video Before It's Gone
items.desc: Many Palm Desert businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks, so requesting preservation quickly can be critical. An attorney in the network can send a preservation letter fast to protect that evidence.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning your recovery can be reduced but not eliminated if you're found partially at fault. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that fairly accounts for shared responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Palm Desert?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city building or park, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. Speaking with an attorney soon after the fall helps make sure this window isn't missed.

items.question: What if I fell partly because I wasn't paying attention?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover damages even if you share some blame for the fall, though your compensation may be reduced by your percentage of fault. This is common in busy retail and resort areas along Highway 111 and El Paseo. An attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: Does it matter that my fall happened at a golf resort or shopping center in Palm Desert?
items.answer: Commercial properties, including the resorts and retail centers common in Palm Desert, are held to a duty to maintain reasonably safe conditions for visitors. This includes addressing spills, uneven walkways, or lighting issues within a reasonable time. An attorney can look into maintenance records and staff schedules to help determine whether that duty was met.
